text:
sophie: PR #8421 is ready for review but blocked on architecture signoff. The change adds request routing rules and a new canary routing policy. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8421

ajay: can you paste the RFC link and a short SLO delta? need to know risk surface before arch eyes

sophie: RFC attached: https://internal.redwood.ai/rfcs/2026-routing-variants. Summary: new routing policy routes 10% of traffic to quantized model variant on Dedicated; fallback to host model on QoS breach. Expected p95 +20ms under steady load.

ben: what are you thinking for canary window and rollback criteria?

sophie: plan in PR: 10% traffic for 6h, monitor p95 latency, 5xx rate, and user-facing error rate. rollback if 5xx > 1% sustained 5m or p95 increases > 50ms for 10m.

maria: who will own the rollout and watch the metrics during the window?

ajay: also add the RFC ID to the PR description and link tests. we need e2e that validates fallback behavior (simulate node OOM)

sophie: added RFC link and e2e note to PR description, tests are in a branch and I'll link once CI passes. tagging @nathan for arch review.

ci-bot: automated check failed — lint error in routing/handler.go: line 142 trailing whitespace

ben: I'll pick up a first pass on code review once lint is fixed. @sophie can you also add a short release-note entry under /docs/releases

sophie: lint fixed and release note added. pushed. thanks.

nathan: LGTM from architecture standpoint. left a comment on the RFC about reducing fallback timeout; otherwise ok. Approved for merge once canary config (traffic percentage + monitoring dashboards) is included in the PR and CI green.

sophie: great — will add the canary dashboard links and wait for CI. merging after arch-approved + successful canary. :thumbsup:
